subject: Orion Labs: regional SKU split and latency tradeoffs for dedicated commitment
messages:

Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask — region split guidance for dedicated commitment

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're at the late-stage procurement step and need to firm up the dedicated capacity ask so we can finalize internal budget and the SOW. High-level requirements:
- Expected peak inference: ~1.2M tokens/day initially; projected to 5M tokens/day in 9 months.
- Latency target: P95 < 250ms for US-facing endpoints; P95 < 300ms for EU; APAC low-latency pilot in Singapore (P95 < 350ms).
- Models: mix of 13B and 70B variants, prefer quantized variants for cost.
- Data residency: EU requirement for a subset of 30% of requests.

Can you recommend a regional SKU split (US/EU/APAC) and associated node counts we should include in the commitment? Procurement wants a concrete tranche proposal they can approve. I've attached our internal demand matrix.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Lee
Head of Infrastructure, Orion Labs

Subject: Re: Initial ask — region split guidance for dedicated commitment

Sarah —

Thanks for the clear matrix, that was helpful. Quick read: your peak profile is bursty with sustained baseline; good candidate for a tranche + burst buffer approach. High-level recommends below — I attached a formal SKU split pdf and a starter Excel with node counts.

Proposed initial tranche (0–6 months):
- US: 12 nodes (mix: 9 x 70B-quantized capacity-equivalent, 3 x 13B for low-latency small requests)
- EU: 4 nodes (to satisfy the 30% EU residency; colocate in Frankfurt; model mix skewed to 13B for cost)
- APAC (Singapore pilot): 2 nodes (burst-only initially)

Burst buffer (shared cross-region): 6 nodes in our reserved pool that can be routed by policy for traffic spikes (costly but keeps latency SLOs during peaks).

Notes / tradeoffs:
- If you need strict P95 < 250ms in APAC, we'll need at least 4 local nodes instead of 2; that doubles APAC committed cost.
- EU data residency can be handled by pinning 30% of traffic to EU nodes; cross-region fallback possible but flagged in the SOW.
- We recommend quantized 4-bit/8-bit profiles on 70B where acceptable to reduce token cost; Rishi can add technical constraints below.

Next steps:
1) Rishi to confirm kernel/kv-cache limits per node for 70B quantized variants.
2) Lauren to provide pricing delta for the tranche vs burst model.
3) If this looks good, we can draft an SOW and DocuSign template for approval.

Ava Chen
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ava@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Initial ask — region split guidance for dedicated commitment

Sarah/Ava —

Couple of technical points to make the SKU guidance actionable:
1) 70B quantized (4-bit) gives ~2.8x token throughput improvement vs float16 on our current kernels for short-context interactive workloads; however, KV cache for long-context (>8k) pushes memory pressure — expect effective throughput drop ~15% at sustained 12k contexts.
2) For your P95 targets:
   - US: 12 nodes should meet P95 < 250ms if average context stays <4k and batching latency is constrained (we can configure continuous batching windows at 20ms).
   - EU: 4 nodes with local caching should hit ~260–300ms P95 depending on mix. Consider an additional EU burst node for regional spikes.
3) Warm-start behavior: We recommend prefix caching for known prompt families; we can pre-warm KV caches during scheduled on-call windows to trim cold-start tails.

Marcus, can you confirm whether the fleet routing policy can reserve 1 of the shared burst nodes purely for EU failover during EMEA business hours?

- Rishi
Principal Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference

Sarah —

Thanks for the details. To make procurement comfortable we need a clear cost comparison: committed tranche pricing vs committed + burst buffer vs fully-committed (no burst). I've populated the attached tab with 12/4/2 node mixes (US/EU/APAC) and two burst sizing options.

High-level pricing deltas (est):
- Committed-only (12/4/2): baseline monthly OPEX = $XXX,XXX (includes support + standard SLAs)
- Committed + burst (12/4/2 + 6 burst): baseline monthly OPEX = +~28% (with burst routing and higher SLA credit availability)
- Fully committed (16/6/4): baseline monthly OPEX = +~55% vs committed-only but reduces routing complexity and gives stronger in-region latency margins.

If you need margin on EU residency (no cross-region fallback), we'll price an EU-only failover node set as a mid-grade option.

Procurement — please identify the internal approver and target sign date; we can align SOW timelines with your fiscal quarter close.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
